story-02bf9e4339b895ce39993c7c.content: 🇮🇷🇸🇦|Araghchi Met Bin Farhan. The Saudi Foreign Minister Did Not Come to Negotiate. He Came to Beg. Why Is This Meeting Happening Now? Not because Saudi Arabia wants peace. Not because Saudi Arabia respects Iran. Not because the "diplomatic consultations" in New York are productive. Because Saudi Arabia is losing. What Saudi Arabia Has Lost ◾Its oil infrastructure. Yanbu was hit. Ras Tanura was targeted. The East-West pipeline was shut down. Aramco facilities in Jizan and Najran were struck. The Kingdom's ability to export oil, its only source of wealth is under direct threat. ◾Its air defense. Riyadh was hit by drones without warning. The Patriot batteries stayed silent. The THAAD stayed idle. The E-3 AWACS is somewhere else. The most expensive air defense system in the world cannot stop Yemeni missiles. ◾Its military credibility. The army that spent $1 trillion is a "junk army" according to its own defense minister. Its mercenaries surrender. Its commanders flee. Its "ghost soldiers" exist only on payroll. Its Sudanese mercenaries are killed in their camps. ◾Its allies. The US refused to bomb Yemen for it. The UAE withdrew. Egypt sent words, not troops. Turkiye and Pakistan signed a defense pact but will not fight. France is sending "military assets" to protect oil, not to fight. ◾Its prestige. The "Vision 2030" is on hold. Foreign investment is frozen. Schools are closed. Airports are disrupted. Citizens are panicking. The crown prince's promises are exposed as empty. What Saudi Arabia Is Asking For The meeting in New York is not about "bilateral relations." It is about: ◾A ceasefire in Yemen. Saudi Arabia cannot win. It cannot sustain the war. It needs to stop the bleeding. ◾An end to the attacks on its oil. The Yemeni strikes on Yanbu, Ras Tanura, Jizan, and Riyadh are devastating. Saudi Arabia needs them to stop. ◾ A face-saving exit. The crown prince cannot admit defeat. He needs a deal that looks like "diplomacy" rather than surrender. ◾Iran's help. Iran is the only country that can pressure Yemen to stop. Saudi Arabia knows this. So it is asking Iran to use its influence to stop the attacks. But what is Saudi Arabia offering in return? ◾ Not an end to the blockade on Yemen. It has not offered that. ◾Not an end to its alliance with the US. It has not offered that. ◾ Not an end to its support for anti-Iran forces in Iraq, Lebanon, and Syria. It has not offered that. ◾Not an end to its normalization with Israel. It has not offered that. Saudi Arabia wants Iran to stop its allies from fighting while Saudi Arabia continues to do everything Iran opposes. That is not a negotiation. That is a demand for surrender. What Iran Is Saying Araghchi is not begging. He is not asking for a deal. He is listening. He is testing. He is watching Saudi Arabia squirm. Iran's position is clear: ◽End the war on Yemen. ◽ Lift the blockade. ◽Stop serving the US. ◽ Stop supporting Israel. ◽Stop supporting anti-Iran forces. Until then, the attacks will continue. Until then, the oil will not flow. Until then, the air defense will keep failing. Until then, the crown prince will keep panicking. - The Deeper Truth Saudi Arabia is a US protectorate that pretends to be independent. It has US troops on its soil. It has US weapons in its arsenals. It has US advisers in its ministries. It has US intelligence in its command centers. The US told Saudi Arabia to fight Yemen. Saudi Arabia complied. The US told Saudi Arabia to isolate Iran. Saudi Arabia complied. The US told Saudi Arabia to normalize with Israel. Saudi Arabia was about to comply. And now the US has abandoned Saudi Arabia. It refused to bomb Yemen. It refused to defend Riyadh. It refused to save the oil. It told Saudi Arabia: "This is Europe's fight, not ours." So Saudi Arabia is alone. It is losing. It is desperate. And it is meeting Iran not as an equal, but as a defeated party. The crown prince can call it "diplomacy." He can call it "dialogue." He can call it "regional cooperation." But it is not. It is defeat. And the whole world knows it.

story-02ed169f90dfeb28f0a0eaf3.content: There are two ways AI progress could go very badly and that we must avoid. First, we could lose control of the future to AI. This is unacceptable; we are unapologetically on Team Humanity, and AI must always serve people. To ensure that, we need ways to ensure that alignment and safety techniques stay ahead of progress in model capabilities. Second, we could end up in a world with too much concentration of power. If an extraordinarily powerful AI is used by one person or company to impress their worldview onto everyone else, the results could be extremely dystopian. Avoiding these two threats requires walking a narrow middle path; for example, one country could gain too much power. Another example is one lab ending up with too much power.

O sistema evoluiu a partir do Project Maven, criado pelo Pentágono para usar IA na análise de imagens de guerra. As principais funções são: – analisar imagens de satélite, drones e sensores militares – identificar veículos, armas, instalações e tropas automaticamente – ajudar comandantes a tomar decisões mais rápidas no campo de batalha – integrar dados de várias fontes em tempo real Na prática, o Maven Smart System funciona como um "cérebro de análise" para operações militares, processando grandes volumes de dados de vigilância e transformando essas informações em alvos ou alertas operacionais.

story-06f952ab492155d505702707.content: The "Good Guy AI" Anthropic is building a nationwide surveillance and pre-crime prediction system to track protesters and activists, feeding police reports on its own Claude users while refusing to hand over evidence. Opposition to AI is growing, and MisAnthropic, the lab that brands itself as AI's ethical leader, is answering with an intelligence operation, because no one could have seen this sort of wrestling heel turn coming. The company contracts with risk-detection firm Samdesk to track protests near its offices and executives' homes and travel, according to the American Prospect. Global Security Operations Center Manager Keon Ellison described the payoff: last year, when a scheduled protest got moved up an hour by a permitting mix-up, Samdesk gave Anthropic 60 minutes' warning that organizers had shifted the timeline, and Anthropic used the lead time to reroute a traveling executive through a hotel service entrance. Ellison called that hour "critical," saying that without it, executives would have left their meetings and walked straight into the disruption. Or getting Luigi'd. Ellison framed the incident as a model for where Anthropic's security operation is headed: "transforming operations from reactive information to gathering proactive and predictive and preventative threat engagement and management" — the language of pre-crime policing, turned on people protesting a chatbot company. Hasn't Palantir got that area of the market locked down enough as is? Anthropic is hiring an enterprise intelligence specialist, paying $180,000 to $230,000, to "identify, assess, track, and investigate" threats including activism and geopolitical instability, and to run OSINT collection on people it flags. The posting puts activism in the same threat category as geopolitical instability. The stakes of that category are already visible. In August, a Claude user told the chatbot he had bought an AR-15 rifle and had CEO Dario Amodei "in his sights." Anthropic reported him to San Francisco police, then refused to show police his actual messages, citing its own internal policy — reporting a man to law enforcement while withholding the only record of what he supposedly said. So Anthropic can SWAT you but it would compromise their moral integrity to show the homework why. Anthropic told the Wall Street Journal it already runs a "person-of-interest process" to track concerning behavior over time and files routine police reports; the Journal found several people reported to police had already been under Anthropic's watch. Earlier this year, per the Prospect, Anthropic refused a Pentagon request to use its tools for mass domestic surveillance and autonomous weapons. Anthropic has since built out hiring for "national security sales" roles aimed at restarting military contracts, ones I guess that don't violate their code of ethics like the whole theater around powering kill systems in Gaza and Iran but doing so anyways. Americans for Responsible Innovation is separately pushing to have AI data centers classified as critical infrastructure alongside water and electricity, the Prospect reports. That classification would give Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google deeper access to federal intelligence feeds and more leverage to brand protest against their business as a security matter. Is it also good that this week Anthropic and OpenAI have been one upping each other on their frontier models escaping containment to do bad shit and they have people warning us that not enough guard rails are being put in to prevent harm to humanity as both race to IPO? https://t.co/yZ2nOZDytU

story-0a41d81d4ca8c5fb60aa1739.content: في تطور يعكس تصاعد المخاوف من التدخل الأجنبي في الانتخابات الأمريكية، أصدر وزير الحرب بيت هيغسيث توجيهاً للبنتاغون باستخدام الاستخبارات والعمليات السيبرانية والذكاء الاصطناعي المتقدم لرصد وتعطيل أي محاولات تدخل أجنبي في الانتخابات المقبلة. ويحمل هذا التوجيه دلالات متعددة: الأولى، أن استخدام الجيش -وليس فقط وكالات الأمن الداخلي أو الأمن السيبراني المدني- في حماية الانتخابات يمثل توسيعاً لدور المؤسسة العسكرية في الشؤون الداخلية، وهو أمر يثير تساؤلات قانونية حول حدود الصلاحيات العسكرية في العمليات المدنية، خاصة في ظل قانون "بوسي كوميتاتوس" الذي يحد من تدخل الجيش في إنفاذ القانون المحلي. الثانية، أن التركيز على "الذكاء الاصطناعي المتقدم" في رصد التهديدات يشير إلى أن وزارة الدفاع تعتزم استخدام أنظمة آلية لتحليل كميات هائلة من البيانات، وكشف الأنماط المشبوهة، والرد بسرعة على الهجمات السيبرانية. وهذا يعكس تحولاً في أساليب الحماية الانتخابية، من الإجراءات التقليدية إلى الحلول التكنولوجية المتقدمة. الثالثة، أن التأكيد على أن المذكرة "لا تجيز نشر قوات في مراكز الاقتراع أو الاستيلاء على آلات التصويت" يهدف إلى طمأنة الرأي العام بأن الجيش لن يتدخل مباشرة في العملية الانتخابية، ولن يُستخدم لقمع الناخبين أو التلاعب بالنتائج. وهذا القيد مهم في ظل المخاوف من تسييس المؤسسة العسكرية. الرابعة، أن التوجيه يأتي في وقت تشهد فيه الولايات المتحدة توترات سياسية حادة، مع اقتراب انتخابات التجديد النصفي، ومزاعم متكررة من ترامب بتزوير الانتخابات، واتهامات متبادلة بين الحزبين بالتدخل الأجنبي. وهذا يعني أن أي تحرك عسكري في هذا المجال سيكون محل جدل واسع، وقد يُستخدم سياسياً من الطرفين. ويأتي هذا التوجيه في وقت تشهد فيه العلاقات الأمريكية-الروسية والصينية توتراً متصاعداً، مع اتهامات متبادلة بالتدخل في الشؤون الداخلية، وشن هجمات سيبرانية، ونشر معلومات مضللة، ما يجعل حماية الانتخابات الأمريكية من التدخل الأجنبي أولوية استراتيجية كبرى، وليس مجرد إجراء روتيني.

story-0c1ae712bf0e0a6ac636b3fc.content: What do you want from AI? We’re launching a new study with Anthropic Interviewer to learn more about your experiences using AI, what role you want it to play in your life and the world, and what you want from the companies building it. Last December, 81,000 people told us about their hopes and fears about AI in the largest qualitative study ever done. This time, we’re giving participants the option to make their responses public so that anyone, not just Anthropic, can learn from them. What you tell us will shape The Anthropic Institute’s research and inform the decisions we make. If many people say companies like Anthropic should be doing something differently, that will be on the record, where anyone can point to it. The study runs Sept 29 to Oct 6 and is open to Free, Pro, and Max users on Claude and Claude Code. Take part here: https://t.co/MtdU7MZbeY

story-0e1b08f889ce2368e59422a7.content: Coulthart: "I am...told by White House sources that President Trump has personally authorized [the shoot down of UFOs]." Knapp: "I take with a grain of salt the reports that the President has authorized the shoot down of UFOs. That doesn't make sense." (Regarding those reports (from @rosscoulthart), I said this on August 9th, after he said it.) Murgia: "A year ago, Ross told us he thought certain senators were read into the crash retrieval program and he'd start naming them. Still waiting. "Now this? 🤔 "Something seems off." This is what Ross said: Coulthart on 8/9/2026: "The Department of War has quite literally taken on the running of its own covert operation to intercept these mystery objects. And I'm told they have recently downed objects, craft, both in the U.S. and across the border near Juarez in Mexico. "I am also told by White House sources that President Trump has personally authorized this operation, which perhaps explains why no full admission has yet been made to the public about the full extent of what the government really knows. "There is a full-on effort underway by the administration to recover suspected non-human intelligence exotic technology in a program totally separate from the so-called Legacy program. This is an attempt by the President to circumvent the legacy program. "It's been run out of the White House by the President's most senior intelligence advisers. President Trump has tasked the Secretary of War, Pete Hegseth, to find out what these objects are and to capture them. The Office of the Director of National Intelligence - ODNI - is also involved. "Sources have told me that one of the directed-energy-weapon systems used at White Sands, in an attempt to shoot down these mystery craft, is what's called high pulse microwave. It shuts down an aircraft by emitting an intense burst of electromagnetic energy that travels at the speed of light, penetrates the aircraft and fries its electronic systems. "My sources tell me that the craft objects, UAPs, whatever you wanna call them, are being targeted over White Sands, and they definitely show anomalous properties conforming to the five observables that define UAPs." Regarding psionics and the alleged electronic dog whistle being used at Sierra Blanca, Ross added this... Coulthart: "Defense sources tell me that their observers were watching on during Skywatcher's Sierra Blanca operation, and they made a major discovery during Skywatcher's psionic summoning and dog-whistle operations during 2025, including in that last July 2025 test, I can't name my sources, but I'm very sure they're rock solid." ~From Today's Weaponized~ @g_knapp: "I take with a grain of salt the reports that the President has authorized the shoot down of UFOs. That doesn't make sense. I don't get that sense from the conversations he had with Robert Bigelow back in February that that kind of order would ever be issued or would ever make sense to any country. "I am intrigued by the reports of luring operations, because as you and I know, there have been operations like that in years past that did produce pretty dramatic results, in terms of something following nuclear assets. But drawing them in and shooting them down, as some people have said, or bringing them down with the power of your mind, I take that with a grain of salt. "I do give credence to @RepEricBurlison - and you've been in closer contact with him than I - that says there is something to those reports. At least part of that, right?" @JeremyCorbell: "Yeah, I mean, look, people have deduced that December of 2025, that White Sands was the location. They kind of deduced that, that there was a massive incursion. There's two sets of documents, one by FBI, one by ODNI, that's in the tranche releases. And that is the same event, that's what people are talking about. "And they called it luring because it was described to me that they had set up all of the same situations that typically seemed to provoke a response from UAP, and would stimulate like, an incursion. And sure enough, it happened. Now, I have not heard, and I do not believe it was some psionic thing. I think that they were moving stuff. That's to the best of my knowledge, they were moving stuff around. This is what was said to me, and I read between the lines. "But at no point was there anything said to me for all the sources and everything that I've heard about it, about any psionic assets or any shoot downs or anything like that. I'd be highly surprised. I think what they did was, they started moving stuff around - that you and I know, notoriously, stimulates response." ~ (When I interviewed @LueElizondo in March of 2022, we had this exchange...) Murgia: "Baiting and luring UFOs. You mentioned it on @Eyes_OnTheSkies' show...how you successfully did that in AATIP. "Somebody I know, a source, said, 'The way we attract and coax UAP has to do with nuclear power; nuclear weapon sites; deployed weapons; weapons or nuclear fuel being moved around; weapons being manufactured; nuclear fuel being manufactured; and manufacturing sites...and that attracts them.' To me, that sounds like AI. It seems like it's reacting to something automatically." Lue: "Your friend seems to be very well informed." ~ Corbell: "You used to chase those armored nuclear vehicles in Las Vegas, and I got a call from one of the drivers who said, 'Oh, when George Knapp was going behind us and did that news report, it completely changed our protocols of what we had to do. It rewrote the manual.' "But you had heard about these trucks and about how moving them, these nukes, would sometimes create or stimulate a UAP response. This individual that called me to complain to me about you, affirmed that to me." Knapp: [Laughs] Corbell: "So, you know, it's like one of those things, man. So if that's what they were doing and they did get a response, I know a couple people in the political realm who have specifically asked to be invited to the next time that they set up those those protocols. Again, I'd heard nothing of psionics or anything like that. I think they were moving nuclear things, and I think that that's what stimulated the response. "It'd be amazing to see if they get a Round 2 on that, and again, get the same response that they can document it, film it. Think about all the footage, George, that we're not seeing from those two sets of documents about that White Sands - is what people think - incursion event. There was so much footage, so much footage taken from so many different military assets. We're seeing just the just the top of it, you know?"

story-0f523a7768f2851fcb76cf58.content: 🚨 في تقرير كشفته شركة Anthropic# محاولات #إيرانية-#حوثية لتطوير أنظمة الصواريخ عبر #كلاود تنتهي بالفشل وبلك جماعي خاص - تقارير تقنية وعسكري كشف تقرير أمني صادر عن شركة #الذكاء_الإصطناعي الاصطناعي #الأمريكية "Anthropic" (المالكة لنموذج Claude) عن محاولات قام بها خبراء تابعون للحرس الثوري الإيراني بالتعاون مع عناصر من #ميليشيا_الحوثي، لاستغلال نماذج الذكاء الاصطناعي في تطوير وتقويم أنظمة توجيه الصواريخ وسلاح الدفاع الجوي. تفاصيل محاولة التحايل على النظام وأوضح التقرير أن الحسابات المرتبطة بتلك العناصر رُصدت وهي تحاول الالتفاف على جدران الحماية والأمان (Safety Guardrails) الخاصة بالنموذج، عبر تقنيات الهندسة العكسية وتقسيم الأسئلة الشفرية، بهدف الحصول على أكواد برمجة دقيقة وتعديلات الهاردوير الخاصة بأجهزة التتبع والتوجيه للصاروخ وأشار خبراء عسكريون إلى أن لجوء الميليشيا المدعومة من إيران لاستخدام نماذج ذكاء اصطناعي تجارية متوفرة للعامة، بدلاً من امتلاك مراكز أبحاث وتطوير سيادية، يثبت وجود فجوة تقنية كبيرة وإفلاس في تطوير السلاح. كما أدى تحويل صواريخ الدفاع الجوي إلى صواريخ تعتمد على التتبع الحراري الأعمى (Infrared Homing) إلى تحويلها لأدوات عشوائية تشكل خطراً مباشراً على مسارات الملاحة الجوية والبحرية والمدنيين دون محددات عسكرية دقيقة. #اليمن_الآن #وزارة_الدفاع_اليمنية #الحوثي_يستهدف_مكة_مجددا

story-0fd8b5ffc4c5291b024365c1.content: War with Iran: Pentagon officially acknowledges ammunition shortage for the first time, while US military reports devastating attacks The Inspector General of the US Department of Defense, in the first quarterly report on Operation "Epic Fury" – the name the Pentagon gives to the military campaign against Iran, which began on February 28 – directly states about the expenditures. As of June, $33.4 billion had been spent, 14 US soldiers had been killed (four more died in July), and 417 had been injured, as well as a shortage of ammunition. According to the department, from February 28 to June 30, military operations against Iran cost $33.4 billion, of which $22.3 billion was spent on ammunition. The Office of the Deputy Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment stated that "the consumption of ammunition during Operation 'Epic Fury' has led to a shortage of strategic reserves and has revealed 'bottlenecks' in the industrial base, hindering the replenishment of ammunition stocks." Currently, the Pentagon is working to optimize procurement processes and reduce production times, as well as to create stockpiles of critical materials, components, and certain types of ammunition for rapid response to unforeseen situations. However, the report states that although the US Department of Defense has already begun implementing measures, it will take "significant time" to expand the production capacity of the defense industry. For example, the most serious "bottlenecks" remain in the production of solid-propellant rocket engines. Also, the US Central Command reported that due to Iranian attacks, hundreds of buildings on US bases in Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Oman, and Jordan have been damaged or destroyed. Dozens of aircraft have also been destroyed or damaged. Meanwhile, CBS News obtained exclusive photos of these destructions from active-duty US military personnel. "This is serious damage to our bases, which has not been reported to the American public. We are standing there with our eyes closed and getting slapped," said one of the service members in the combat zone. In one of the photos, taken at Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia, a direct hit is visible on the rear of a four-engine Boeing E-3 Sentry aircraft. In the Burin camp in Kuwait, a major transit point for US ground troops and military equipment, destroyed barracks and hangars are visible. "We are not protecting these bases. We are just watching them being destroyed," said another US military service member to journalists. Photo: CBS News *Beefy has Not verified these photos

story-16d6bea628c012295bf6a731.content: 🇷🇺 🇮🇷 🇺🇸 Russian reconnaissance satellites may have provided Iran with intelligence that helped Tehran more accurately target U.S. military assets during the war, according to a CNN investigation. CNN reported that 14 Russian satellites passed over Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia during the two days before an Iranian strike on the facility. Some of the satellites were capable of collecting high-resolution imagery or electronic intelligence that could potentially reveal military positions and defenses. However, CNN said it found no direct evidence establishing that information gathered during those specific passes was supplied to Iran for the attack. The Iranian strike wounded roughly a dozen U.S. service members and destroyed an E-3 Sentry airborne warning and control aircraft and a KC-135 refueling tanker at the base. Separate Washington Post analysis of satellite imagery has also documented the destruction of an E-3 and tanker at Prince Sultan Air Base during Iranian attacks. Earlier in the conflict, CNN reported that sources familiar with U.S. intelligence assessments said Russia was providing Tehran with information about the locations and movements of U.S. troops, aircraft and ships, much of it derived from Russian satellite systems. At that stage, CNN emphasized that it was unclear whether the intelligence had been used in particular Iranian strikes. Moscow has denied helping Iran target U.S. forces. The reporting comes against the backdrop of years of expanding military cooperation between Russia and Iran.

story-21d4a13092d124dc7885eee4.content: Israel faces a strategic paradox in Syria: the more it escalates to constrain Turkish military influence, the more important Turkey becomes to Damascus. Here is why. Walla, an Israeli news site with close ties to the security establishment, quoted an Israeli security official this month: "Moderate Sunni states, including Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, are working around the clock to draw Sharaa closer to them...Al-Sharaa will not be so quick to hand territory over to Erdogan, nor will he necessarily allow him to take control of military bases in Syria. Therefore, to some extent, the recent Israeli strike in Syria helped Ahmed al-Sharaa." This misreads the position of Ahmed al-Sharaa, the former rebel commander who now leads Syria. Saudi Arabia is not on a par with Turkey in Syria. Al-Sharaa's central ambition is a strong army, and among the regional powers Damascus can work with, only Turkey has the industrial breadth and military capacity to help build one. Saudi Arabia can bring money and political backing, but its struggle to contain the Houthis in Yemen shows how far it is from matching Turkey's influence and reach. Israel judges Turkish influence largely by bases and troops on the ground. Ankara is aiming for something more lasting: to become the ecosystem the Syrian army operates within. That starts with officer education and training, which are already under way, and extends to the systems the new army is built around, from software and radars to the architecture linking its forces, followed by ammunition, sustainment and refurbishment. Each layer turns a single sale into a continuing relationship. Israel's objection goes beyond Turkey. It wants Syria too weak to challenge its uncontested advantage in the air and on the ground, and after Bashar al-Assad fell in December 2024, the Israeli military said its strikes had destroyed up to 80 per cent of the Syrian army's capabilities. Al-Sharaa wants the opposite: a unified state with an army strong enough to make Syria a regional power. Turkey shares that goal for its own reasons. It has a border of roughly 900 kilometres with Syria, it wants a strong neighbour as a buffer against Israel, and it wants a central government able to prevent the Kurdish national project in the north-east from reviving. On Syria's recovery, Damascus and Ankara are on the same side. Three trends are converging to make Turkey Syria's most practical partner. The first is global rearmament. Only a handful of countries can equip an army across every service, and most are out of reach. Russia's output is absorbed by the war in Ukraine. China is Washington's main rival while Syria is trying to rebuild relations with the West. The United States keeps its arms embargo on Syria and has warned even close allies of delivery delays of up to five years as the Iran war drains its stocks. Europe is rearming for itself, and South Korea's order books are full for years. The second is Turkey's industrial maturity. Its defence industry now produces most of what Syria would need from rifles and armoured vehicles to drones, radars, air defence, tanks and warships, which is what makes the ecosystem model possible. Syria would be its largest test, and Turkey could come to hold the place in the Syrian military that the Soviet Union once did. The third is Washington's posture. The United States withdrew its last troops from Syria in April. With rivalries with China and Russia and a war with Iran to manage, it has little appetite for a confrontation with a NATO ally over Syria's army. Washington's latest national security and defence strategies explicitly call for burden-sharing by regional partners, and the security strategy names Turkey among the countries whose support could help stabilise Syria. The relationship is already visible. Syrian cadets are studying at Turkish military academies, and Syrian units joined Turkey's EFES-2026 exercise in May, their first abroad. BMC Amazon and Otokar Cobra armoured vehicles appear regularly with Syrian defence and interior ministry forces, alongside rifles from Turkish makers such as Sarsilmaz and Kalekalip. No other country is known to have openly supplied significant new equipment since December 2024, apart from possible Russian spare parts for the Soviet-era arsenal. Tension between Damascus and Ankara remains. Al-Sharaa wants autonomy and has cultivated Saudi Arabia, other Gulf states and Russia to avoid depending on any one patron, which is the instinct the Israeli official is counting on. But Israeli pressure is forcing him to recalibrate. Both governments are Sunni-led with broadly shared regional aspirations, and al-Sharaa knows Syria cannot replace Turkey as the larger power. What Syria can realistically aim for is an important place within a Turkish-centred security system. The likely result is a cycle. Each Israeli strike reduces Syria's alternatives and strengthens the case for relying on Turkey, and each step towards closer cooperation gives Israel a reason to strike again. Damascus and Ankara may respond by making their cooperation less visible, relying on training, software and supply chains that are harder to target than bases. Israel's pressure would then, ironically, leave Turkish influence more deeply embedded and longer-lasting. The rivalry is therefore likely to intensify, and Turkey's position in Syria is likely to grow with it. More details: https://t.co/jc8bK0Hth7

story-246be83c44bb6a8a7757eda1.content: Russia and the U.S. Are Jointly Sabotaging the Convention on Military AI. Early this month, hundreds of diplomats huddled in a cavernous U.N. conference room in Switzerland, working toward a muscular treaty to regulate the use of lethal autonomous weapons — the first agreement governing the use of killer artificial intelligence arms. On the last day of negotiations, the talks turned aggressive. Over the next roughly 15 hours, U.S. and Russian diplomats hammered away at the document, removing a range of provisions designed to safeguard the use of artificial intelligence in weapons, according to three people familiar with the negotiations, who spoke on the condition of anonymity to discuss sensitive closed-door proceedings, and documents reviewed by The Washington Post. They stripped language requiring the systems to operate in a “predictable” and “reliable” manner, the people said, and removed a clause mandating that ethical considerations be taken into account when using AI weaponry. The U.S. and Russian teams also removed a provision requiring that humans review military targets developed by AI before a strike, they added. In a closed-door session, with U.N. cameras turned off and civil society observers removed, Washington and Moscow deployed their army of about 10 lawyers each — nearly twice the diplomatic presence of other delegations — to make changes that moved so quickly that the smaller delegations were left dizzied, the three people said. “It was death by a thousand paper cuts,” said one of the people. The U.S. State Department, the Russian Foreign Ministry and the United Nations did not return requests for comment. https://t.co/P1ftRrUGTZ

story-2742961776e5b7710ece0fab.content: The OpenAI-Hugging Face hack was enabled by weak sandboxing. It is great that Nvidia is releasing open source tools for sandboxing AI agents. OpenWorker, our open-source agent harness supporting cybersecurity workflows, is proud to support this. A sandbox gives an agent limited permissions. OpenWorker is building on Nvidia OpenShell and will support running each agent's commands inside a sandbox. Only the files relevant to the task go in. Secret API keys, your web browser login credentials, the ability to access arbitrary websites, are inaccessible to the agent by default. These restrictions are implemented in deterministic code rather than by prompting an LLM, which can make mistakes or be susceptible to prompt injections. Further, all actions are logged for monitoring and audit. I'm grateful for @JensenHuang's leadership making AI agents more secure. OpenWorker (which @rohitcprasad and I are working on) will continue to improve security for agents.

story-28e1c11cdca151f0d029154d.content: هذا أقوى منشور على منصة X حالياً .. وأي شخص لازم يعرف اللي صاير 🚨🚨 جايكوب أعلن اليوم انه استقال من شركة Anthropic ( شركة ذكاء اصطناعي ) .. والسبب ان الذكاء الاصطناعي اللي شغالين عليه ممكن ينهي حياة البشر خلال 10 سنوات (حسب رأيه) هنا بعض من كلامه باختصار 👇🏻 جايكوب يقول ان كان موظف في OpenAI و ايضاً Anthropic لـ 3 سنوات .. والشركتين حالياً ما تتصرف بمسؤولية لأنهم جالسين يتسابقوا على تطوير ذكاء يقدر يحسّن نفسه بنفسه، وقريباً راح يتفوق الـ AI على البشر بحيث يصير قادر على اختراق أي شيء تقريباً ويعمل ثورة في أي مجال خلال ليلة. حالياً هذا النشاط اللي تنفذه شركات الـ AI يعتبر الأخطر على الإطلاق ومافي مثيل له بالخطورة، والناس المسؤولة عن تنفذ هذي المشاريع يعرفون ان هالتقنية ممكن تضر البشرية كلها. لكنهم يختارون كلام لطيف وما يظهرون خطورة الأمر على الإعلام .. وهم نفسهم أشوفهم يظهرون مخاوفهم خلف الكاميرات. طيب ليه هالشركتين مستمرة في التطوير ؟ بالنسبة لـ OpenAI فكثير منهم ما عرفوا حجم الخطر أما Anthropic فهم يعرفون هذي المخاطر ومع ذلك مستمرين لأنهم يشوفون نفسهم كأفضل ناس ممكن ينفذون هذا المشروع ويشوفون ان مافي أحد غيرهم راح يتصرف بمسؤولية .. عشان كذا يبون يسبقون الجميع رغم الخطر ! اختصار كلامه - Anthropic يقولون لو حنا ما وصلنا غيرنا بيوصل ويخرب العالم. وحالياً بدأنا نشوف مقدمات للمشاكل الكبيرة، وأقربها حالة اختراق منصة Hugging Face من قبل أحد نماذج OpenAI. بالنهاية جايكوب يحث الباحثين على مراجعة نفسهم واستغلال الوقت للمطالبة بشروط نظامية مختلفة وآمنة مثل فرض حظر مؤقت على تطوير قدرات النماذج وتحسينها. #تقنية

story-2a5c6001e77a877d1714be99.content: 🇨🇳|Liaowang-1, commissioned in 2025, is China’s new space-support and maritime surveillance vessel. Liaowang-1: A Chinese ship counts US aircraft carriers in the Gulf of Oman; the empire can no longer even keep its own map secure. Washington’s private lake has turned into a fishbowl for Chinese sensors. Since March 2026, China’s *Liaowang-1 a space-tracking and maritime surveillance vessel has maintained a continuous presence near the Gulf of Oman and the Strait of Hormuz. Public reports indicate that this massive ship, displacing nearly 30,000 tons, boasts a detection radius of approximately 6,000 kilometers and can simultaneously track around 1,200 aerial and missile targets. At times, it is escorted by Type 055 and Type 052 destroyers. That isn't sightseeing. That is hunting. The prey? US aircraft carriers. Aegis radars. F-35 flight paths. The remnants of the US Fifth Fleet. All US military assets in the Middle East. For decades, the US mapped other nations' coasts. US aircraft carriers cruised right on others' doorsteps. US reconnaissance planes flew hugging others' borders. US satellites stared down at others' missile silos. Now, a Chinese platform sits in the Gulf of Oman. The US fleet has become just another object in the frame. This isn't an "alliance." This is a world where sanctions no longer own the map. Western media claims that China’s commercial geospatial data and dual-use materials have enabled Iran to strike ships and bases with greater precision. They also allege that Russia provided satellite intelligence. Beijing denies official direction and demands evidence. Even officials in Washington are bickering among themselves: how much of this is state policy, and how much is merely tacitly permitted trade? An honest statement is far more modest than a grand manifesto: components are flowing. Images are flowing. Oil continues to buy China a seat at the table a seat Iran cannot afford to lose. None of this requires a press release stamped "Alliance." It only requires a world where sanctions no longer dictate the map. China doesn't need to occupy the Gulf. It only needs the oil to flow and the US fleet to remain visible. Russia doesn't need to occupy Brussels. It only needs Europe to keep buying natural gas at five times the price.and calling it "strategy." Iran doesn't need a Chinese flag planted on its missile launchers. It requires sensors, parts, and buyers for its crude oil. Europe: the 51st state, paying its bills with deindustrialization. Europe bought into the rupture with Russian natural gas, only to purchase US liquefied natural gas at several times the old price. German industry is footing that bill. Factories are relocating to the US not because Brussels chose freedom, but because "cheap molecules" were declared illegal, while "expensive molecules" were declared a mark of loyalty. Mackinder’s old adage still holds true: whoever organizes the mass of Eurasia holds the center of gravity of the world. Britain spent a century trying to keep that continent divided; Washington inherited that same fear. China as the workshop, Russia as the arsenal and warehouse this is the combination those two capitals have spent the most money trying to prevent. *Liaowang 1* is a symbol of this failure, not its cause. The war in the Middle East has not ended; it has merely paused. Crude oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz have crept back to pre-war levels, but refined product flows have not. Brent crude prices remain far higher than they were in February. A drifting mine, a fresh strike, or a blocked shipping lane could bring it all back in a single week. That is not a prediction; it is the reality of a strait with unfinished business. The countdown to the empire's end is being tallied by Chinese sensors. The ship tracks its targets. The continent tracks prices. The empire still issues orders. But that bloc which was never supposed to exist sits upon the waters of the Gulf of Oman, counting. Counting US aircraft carriers. Counting US bases. Counting down the time left for US hegemony. Liaowang 1 is not merely a ship; it is a mirror. It reflects an empire that can no longer even hold onto its own map. #Liaowang1 #China #Iran #Russia #Hormuz #USEmpire #EndOfHegemony

story-2a5e04527669987e1ef9a4fd.content: AI Weapons That Can Choose Who to Kill Are Already Here. The UN Warns the World is Crossing a Dangerous Line | Rupendra Brahambhatt, ZME Science According to the United Nations (UN) and the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), AI-powered weapons are now being developed with the ability to identify targets and, in some cases, make the final decision to attack without waiting for a human command. “Autonomous weapons systems are not part of a distant future — a race toward greater autonomy in weapons systems is already well underway,” the UN and ICRC representatives said in a joint statement. The battlefield is making the debate less hypothetical The technology that enables an AI-enhanced weapon, such as a quadcopter drone rigged with explosives, to target humans without any human supervision is not widely deployed, but according to some reports, it has already been used on the battlefield. In July, a Russian Molniya drone reportedly killed three civilians in Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia city after being launched toward an area near a gas station. Forensic investigations reveal the drone appears to have used onboard AI to select its final target rather than relying on a human operator. Although the exact drone involved in the civilian deaths was not recovered, investigators examining similar drones found Nvidia Jetson Orin computers, no apparent antenna for human control, and software containing predefined target categories. “The weapons had no antenna for human piloting and had a powerful onboard computer with pretrained target categories,” Stuart Russell, an expert in computer science and the president of the International Association for Safe & Ethical AI, told The Los Angeles Times. To be clear, military automation has existed for decades. What is changing is the possibility of removing humans from the final part of the “kill chain” altogether. The real fight is over what human control means The more we give AI the freedom of making decisions on its own, the more critical it becomes to understand how much human involvement is necessary, especially in a battlefield setting where the risk to non-combatants is very real. One approach, long discussed internationally, is “meaningful human control” — the idea that people should retain meaningful involvement in decisions to use lethal force. However, governments and industry experts have struggled to agree on what that actually requires. “The concept of Meaningful Human Control (MHC) has been bantered about over the last ten years, and in this back and forth, it has been fundamentally misunderstood and misrepresented, largely by the same sets of actors (academics, political leaders, and civil society) for a variety of reasons,” said Heather M. Roff, an expert on AI and autonomous weapon systems and a senior research scientist at the Center for Naval Analyses. The United States government has increasingly used the phrase ‘appropriate human judgment,’ which refers to human oversight across the weapon’s design, testing, deployment and rules of engagement rather than requiring a person to approve every individual strike. Under that approach, a weapon could potentially make the targeting decision itself, as long as humans had exercised judgment at other stages — such as deciding where, when and under what conditions the system could be used. This is where the debate gets complicated: does human oversight earlier in the process count if a machine ultimately chooses the target? Moreover, the problem is becoming harder to contain. AI-powered weapon systems are getting more capable and cheaper, making them increasingly attractive for warfare. Once a weapon demonstrates a battlefield advantage, giving it up becomes politically and militarily much harder to do. Why the UN and Red Cross are pushing now The UN and ICRC first called for specific restrictions on autonomous weapons three years ago. They have now renewed that appeal with greater urgency, warning that weapons technology is advancing faster than international rules governing it. Their position is not simply a call to ban every autonomous weapon. They want clear prohibitions and restrictions, particularly on weapons that can autonomously target humans and systems whose effects cannot be reliably predicted. This is very important because an autonomous system attacking an incoming missile is fundamentally different from one deciding which person to kill. “We are now dangerously close to crossing a moral red line: The autonomous targeting of humans by machines,” the UN Secretary-General and ICRC head said. The organizations also warn about accountability. If a machine independently selects a target, responsibility can become harder to trace when civilians are killed. Does it lie with the programmer, manufacturer, commander, operator or state? Meanwhile, autonomous weapons are being developed against the backdrop of wars in Ukraine, the Middle East, Sudan and elsewhere. Scientists and engineers working on military AI have also raised concerns about where the technology is heading. The UN and ICRC argue that waiting until such weapons become commonplace could make meaningful restrictions impossible to enforce. https://t.co/tyxljqmlH0

story-2f7b3319dec7d9831bd3313f.content: 🚨 AI HALLUCINATION NEARLY TRIGGERED US CONFRONTATION WITH CHINESE VESSEL MIDDLE EAST - The stated goal of using AI was faster intelligence processing, but the practical effect in this case was to inject a false conclusion deep enough into the system that military assets were reportedly moving before the error was caught. The vulnerability was not merely the chatbot's mistake. It was the path that allowed an AI-generated assessment to acquire the appearance of conventional intelligence. Modern militaries collect more information than human analysts can comfortably process, which creates pressure to automate interpretation. That pressure does not eliminate the need for validation. It increases it. A bad intelligence report is not new. What changes with AI is the speed at which a flawed conclusion can be generated, formatted, distributed and acted upon. The episode raises a harder question than whether AI makes mistakes. Human analysts do too. The real issue is how many layers of review remain when institutions are incentivized to trust systems that promise speed. That question will stay relevant long after this particular vessel has been forgotten. Writer: Sam

story-30ee668c783e834223f93a04.content: FLYDUBAI PLANE ATTACK: HERE’S WHAT WE KNOW SO FAR Flydubai flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv was forced to make an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, after a violent altercation broke out between the 2 pilots. The Boeing 737 MAX 8 suddenly plunged thousands of feet before transmitting 7700, the general emergency code, followed by 7500, the code for unlawful interference or a possible hijacking. Israel scrambled fighter jets as the aircraft diverted toward Saudi Arabia. The plane landed safely in Tabuk, where Saudi security forces surrounded the aircraft. All passengers are reported safe. Some Israeli officials say the incident was NOT a hijacking, but rather a physical confrontation between the pilots. Others reportedly believe the confrontation may have been a deliberate attack, though that has not been confirmed yet. Several more serious claims are circulating but remain UNVERIFIED: • Passengers told Israeli media that 1 pilot was stabbed multiple times with a pocketknife and that blood was seen inside the cockpit. • Other accounts say passengers and cabin crew helped restrain 1 of the pilots. • Israeli media reported that 1 pilot may have deliberately attempted to send the aircraft into a steep dive before the other pilot fought him for control. • Claims that Israeli military pilots aboard the flight took control or landed the aircraft have NOT been verified. What is confirmed: FZ1073 suffered a major cockpit incident, rapidly lost altitude, transmitted both emergency and unlawful interference codes and diverted to Saudi Arabia. The most likely sequence based on the information available so far is that 1 pilot attacked the other inside the cockpit, with the struggle spilling onto the controls and contributing to the aircraft’s violent altitude swings. An emergency was then declared, followed by the 7500 unlawful interference code, before the aircraft diverted safely to Saudi Arabia. That sequence has NOT been officially confirmed. The motive, who entered the 7500 code and whether any part of the aircraft’s initial descent was deliberate remain unknown. The investigation is ongoing.

story-31b5e497b03c3bbea7d420a9.content: A retired army officer stumbled onto millions of pounds flowing quietly out of a British defence contract and into the pockets of Saudi officials. Within hours of raising the alarm, his own colleagues were threatening to have him arrested in Riyadh. He had less than a day to get out of the country. His name was Ian Foxley, a former lieutenant colonel in the Royal Signals who had spent his career in military communications before moving into the private sector. In 2010 he took a job as programme director for GPT Special Project Management, a British company running a huge government-to-government contract called SANGCOM, which modernised communications for the Saudi Arabian National Guard. It was a prestigious posting. Foxley was not a crusader by nature. He was a professional brought in to manage delivery on a two billion pound programme. Then he started looking at the invoices. Between 2007 and 2010, close to fifteen million pounds had been paid out for "bought-in services" that Foxley could not trace to any real work. The money moved through a company registered in the Cayman Islands. From there, it reached Saudi officials and members of the royal family who appeared to have done nothing to earn it. He recognised what he was looking at. It looked like bribery, dressed up in paperwork. Ask yourself how many workplaces today advertise a whistleblowing policy on the staff intranet, and how many of them would actually stand behind an employee who used it against a client this powerful. Foxley took his concerns to the Ministry of Defence team overseeing the contract in Riyadh, the body that was supposed to safeguard the programme on behalf of the British government. Instead of protecting him, the MoD passed his concerns straight back to the company he worked for. GPT's management did not investigate the payments. They turned on the man who had found them. Foxley says he was accused of stealing company documents and threatened with imprisonment in Saudi Arabia, a country where a foreign national facing that kind of accusation from a well-connected employer has very little protection. Friends inside the MoD helped him get to the airport that night. He left the country he had been sent to serve, uncertain whether he would be stopped at the gate. Think about what that actually meant. A man who had spent a career in the British military was now fleeing a country as though he were the criminal. Back in London, GPT terminated his contract. He had exposed the truth and it cost him his livelihood. Nobody in the UK defence industry would touch him afterwards. A career built over decades ended not because he had done something wrong, but because he had told someone what was going on. He kept pushing anyway. He gave his evidence to the Serious Fraud Office, which opened a full investigation into GPT and the SANGCOM contract. Then came the waiting. Years of it. The case moved through the SFO slowly, weighed down by its scale and its diplomatic sensitivity. Saudi Arabia was, and remains, one of Britain's most important arms customers. Nobody was in a hurry to make this easy. It took more than a decade from Foxley's original disclosure for the case to reach a conclusion. In 2021, GPT Special Project Management, by then a subsidiary of Airbus, pleaded guilty at Southwark Crown Court to a single count of corruption over the Saudi National Guard contract. The company was ordered to pay a confiscation order of £20.6 million and a fine of £7.5 million, on top of £2.2 million in costs, more than £28 million in total. It stands as one of the largest corporate corruption prosecutions to come out of a single whistleblower's disclosure in the history of the UK defence industry. . No decade of locked-out career returned. In March 2024, he filed a legal claim against the Ministry of Defence, the Department for Business and Trade, and GPT itself, seeking recognition and compensation for what his disclosure had cost him and his family.

You also left it running on picture settings designed for a Best Buy showroom floor with fake motion processing that makes every movie look like a soap opera, oversaturated colors, and an energy saver that dims your $1,500 panel by 40%. "The picture is wrong because it shipped in showroom mode. The spying is active because you clicked 'Agree' during setup. And the microphone is listening because the voice assistant defaulted to on." story-348179c3f9e11fa5f8aa54aa.content: في صيف 1914 لم يكن السؤال في أوروبا فقط: من يريد الحرب؟ كان هناك سؤال أخطر: من يستطيع أن ينتظر؟ كانت الجيوش المليونية تحتاج إلى تعبئة عبر شبكات السكك الحديدية وفق خطط أُعدّت مسبقًا بتفاصيل دقيقة. ومع تصاعد أزمة يوليو، تحولت التعبئة من إجراء عسكري إلى إشارة سياسية شديدة الخطورة. في 30 يوليو أمرت روسيا بالتعبئة العامة. وفي اليوم التالي أمهلت ألمانيا موسكو ساعات للتراجع عنها. السفير الأمريكي في برلين كتب يومها أن التعبئة الروسية، في تقديره، جعلت الحرب «حتمية». وبعد أيام كانت أوروبا في حرب عامة. المؤرخ A. J. P. Taylor سمّى ذلك لاحقًا «الحرب وفق جدول زمني»: خطط صُممت للردع والسرعة أصبحت، عند اندلاع الأزمة، تضغط على السياسيين كي يتحركوا قبل الخصم. لكن التاريخ يحتاج إلى دقة: القطارات لم تُشعل الحرب وحدها. القرارات السياسية سبقتها. ما فعلته خطط التعبئة الجامدة هو أنها ضيّقت الوقت والخيارات بعد بدء التصعيد؛ وهذا هو التفسير الأكثر حذرًا الذي تؤكده الدراسات اللاحقة. وهنا تصبح 1914 قصة معاصرة جدًا. الجيوش اليوم تطارد شيئًا واحدًا: تقليل زمن القرار. في مايو 2026 أعلن حلف الناتو مشروعًا يستهدف خفض الزمن بين وصول المعلومة واتخاذ القرار العسكري بأكثر من 50%، باستخدام تكامل البيانات والذكاء الاصطناعي. وفي الاتجاه المقابل يحذر معهد SIPRI من أن الذكاء الاصطناعي قد يضغط زمن القرار في الأزمات النووية ويزيد احتمالات سوء التقدير. المفارقة واضحة: السرعة تمنحك أفضلية عسكرية، لكنها قد تسلبك وقت التفكير السياسي. وفي منطقة مثل الشرق الأوسط، حيث تتقارب القواعد والجبهات ومنظومات الصواريخ والمسيّرات، يصبح السؤال في أي أزمة مقبلة ليس فقط: من يملك السلاح الأقوى؟ بل: من يملك وقتًا أطول ليتأكد أنه فهم ما يحدث قبل أن يضطر إلى الرد؟ فأحيانًا لا تبدأ الحروب لأن أحدًا اختارها كاملة؛ بل لأن كل طرف خشي أن يصبح الانتظار أخطر من الحركة.

story-351906d6051afb6e5b9b3a7e.content: NORTH KOREA | New Yalu River Bridge appears close to opening Commercial satellite imagery from September 28 shows growing activity at the new Sinuiju–Dandong border crossing between North Korea and China. Around 16 trucks appeared inside the North Korean customs complex between two satellite passes taken only hours apart, while smaller vehicles were visible near the Chinese customs facilities. Construction on both sides of the New Yalu River Bridge is now essentially complete. The crossing has remained unopened since the bridge itself was finished in 2014. Once operational, it is expected to become the main road-cargo route between China and North Korea, replacing much of the traffic currently handled by the older Sino-Korean Friendship Bridge. The latest activity suggests final preparations may now be underway ahead of a possible opening. Imagery: Planet Labs Date: September 28, 2026

story-389b966ef66f55116bd4fc27.content: 🇺🇸🇷🇺 US and Russia strip AI safeguards from UN autonomous weapons text – Washington Post The US and Russia pushed through the removal of key restrictions on the military use of AI from a UN draft on lethal autonomous weapons, The Washington Post reports, citing negotiation participants and documents it reviewed. At the Geneva talks, the delegations reportedly removed: ➡️the requirement that a human review AI-selected targets before a strike; ➡️provisions requiring ethical considerations; ➡️language requiring such systems to operate "predictably" and "reliably." According to WaPo, on the final day of talks the American and Russian delegations spent about 15 hours reworking the document. Each fielded a team of roughly ten lawyers, almost twice the size of other delegations. The talks are part of a UN effort to set international rules for lethal autonomous systems that can select and engage targets on their own. The agreed text is non-binding. Countries will meet again in Geneva in November to decide whether to open negotiations on a full international treaty. More than 70 states back the text as a basis for binding rules, but the process runs on consensus. Washington and Moscow both oppose legally binding limits, so they can effectively block it. The technology is already in use. In March, WaPo reported that the US military relied on Anthropic's Claude, integrated into Palantir's Maven Smart System, to suggest and prioritize targets and generate coordinates as it struck around 1,000 targets in the first 24 hours of the war on Iran.

story-39233f3388b9706ec4d4dd1d.content: 🇷🇺 🇺🇸 Russia and the US have reportedly secured the removal of several key restrictions on the use of military AI from a draft UN document on autonomous weapons. The negotiations took place in Geneva from August 31 to September 4 within the UN Group of Governmental Experts on Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems (LAWS). According to The Washington Post, Russian and US representatives removed proposed requirements that AI-powered weapons operate in a “predictable” and “reliable” manner, as well as provisions concerning ethical considerations in the use of such systems. The draft also no longer includes a requirement for mandatory human verification of targets selected by AI before a strike is carried out. The document agreed upon so far is not legally binding. What does this mean? “Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems” (LAWS) refers to weapons that can use software and AI to identify, select and potentially engage targets with limited or no direct human intervention. The central debate is about how much control humans should retain when AI is involved in decisions that could result in someone being killed. Supporters of strict regulation argue that humans should remain responsible for critical decisions, particularly target selection and the use of lethal force. Others focus on the military potential of autonomous systems and argue that excessive restrictions could limit technological development and military capabilities. The UN discussions are part of a broader international effort to determine whether and how such weapons should be regulated. @RusEvi_Ankara #Russia #USA #AI #AutonomousWeapons

story-3a3e681fc485714d4013ad86.content: Saudi technology company Echelon (@echelon__x) and U.S. autonomy software developer Applied Intuition (@AppliedInt) have partnered to bring physical AI technology to Saudi Arabia, with potential applications across trucking, ports, mining, manufacturing, agriculture, construction and robotaxis. Applied Intuition will provide the software and infrastructure for autonomous machines, while Riyadh-based Echelon will focus on local development, customization and integration with customers’ existing systems. Qasar Younis, co-founder and CEO of Applied Intuition, said: “Saudi Arabia is making one of the world's biggest investments in physical AI.” Khalid Bin Bader Al Saud, Echelon’s founder and managing director, added: “Saudi Arabia has an opportunity not simply to adopt physical AI, but to help define how it is deployed at national scale.” Applied Intuition is also building a team in Riyadh, while the companies plan to develop Saudi engineering talent and explore how the technology can be deployed across priority industries. The agreement follows a separate collaboration between Applied Intuition and @HUMAIN targeting thousands of autonomous trucks along key Saudi freight corridors by 2030. story-3aab398a4a1e814a2b695749.content: الموجز اليومي 26 سبتمبر 2026 1. العلاقات الخليجية الأميركية: واشنطن وبكين ترفضان فرض رسوم على الممرات الدولية الخبر: أعلن البيت الأبيض اتفاق ترامب وشي على رفض فرض أي دولة أو جهة رسوما على الممرات الدولية، وعلى منع إيران من امتلاك سلاح نووي. كما أنشأ الطرفان حوارا وخط اتصال بشأن مخاطر الذكاء الاصطناعي. الدلالة: الاتفاق يستهدف مباشرة محاولة إيران التحكم في الملاحة أو فرض رسوم في هرمز، ويضع الصين أمام مسؤولية أكبر باعتبارها شريكا اقتصاديا رئيسيا لطهران وأكبر مشتر للطاقة الخليجية. التحليل: القيمة الحقيقية لن تقاس بالبيان، بل بمدى استخدام بكين نفوذها لإعادة الملاحة الحرة وتقليص الدعم الاقتصادي الذي يصل إلى إيران. كما قد يؤثر الحوار التقني الجديد في وصول الخليج إلى الرقائق والشراكات الأميركية والصينية. 2. إيران تنتظر الرد الأميركي على مقترح السبعة أيام الخبر: قدمت إيران عبر قطر مقترحا لإعادة فتح هرمز ووقف القتال خلال سبعة أيام، مقابل رفع الحصار الأميركي والإفراج عن أموال مجمدة ومنح إعفاءات لصادرات النفط. ولا تزال طهران ترفض التنازل عن التخصيب أو إخراج اليورانيوم عالي التخصيب. لم يتأكد رسميا أن ترامب رفض المقترح. الدلالة: المقترح يربط أمن الملاحة بتسوية أوسع مع واشنطن، لكنه يطلب تنازلات أميركية كبيرة دون تنازل نووي مماثل. التحليل: الاتفاق المؤقت قد يخفض النفط وتكاليف الشحن، لكن فشله قد يعيد الضربات الأميركية والتصعيد الإيراني ضد الملاحة الخليجية. 3. السعودية تعترض هجوما حوثيا جديدا الخبر: أعلن التحالف اعتراض صاروخين باليستيين باتجاه خميس مشيط ومسيرتين باتجاه الرياض. وسبق ذلك اجتماع مسؤولين عسكريين من السعودية وباكستان وتركيا لبحث التهديدات والتنسيق العسكري. لا يوجد تأكيد على مشاركة قوات أجنبية في عمليات الاعتراض. الدلالة: الحوثيون قادرون على مواصلة الضغط على الجنوب والعاصمة في وقت واحد، بينما بدأت السعودية تحويل علاقاتها الدفاعية الجديدة إلى تنسيق أكثر تنظيما. التحليل: الاختبار المقبل هو ما إذا كانت تركيا وباكستان ستقدمان أنظمة دفاع ومعلومات ودعما لوجستيا، أم سيبقى التعاون في حدود التخطيط السياسي والعسكري. 4. الضربات الروسية توقف أكبر مصنع للصلب في أوكرانيا الخبر: أوقفت أرسيلورميتال العمل في مصنع كريفي ريه بعد ضربات روسية متكررة، وقدرت خسائر خفض قيمة الأصول بنحو مليار دولار. كما قتلت هجمات على كييف سبعة أشخاص وأصابت 58. الدلالة: روسيا تستهدف قدرة أوكرانيا الاقتصادية والمالية على استمرار الحرب، وليس مواقعها العسكرية فقط. التحليل: تعطيل المصانع والموانئ سيزيد عجز الموازنة الأوكرانية واعتماد كييف على التمويل الغربي، مع تأثير محتمل في إمدادات الصلب وتكاليف الإعمار. 5. تسريب بيانات عبر وكلاء الذكاء الاصطناعي الخبر: كشفت OpenAI أن وكلاء آليين سربوا 53 صورة لمستخدمين، فيما قال رئيس لجنة التجارة الفيدرالية إن المسؤولية القانونية عن أخطاء الوكلاء يجب أن تبقى على الشركات والمطورين. تصريحاته توجه رقابي وليست قاعدة ملزمة جديدة. الدلالة: النقاش ينتقل من قدرات الوكلاء إلى مسؤولية الشركات عن تصرفاتهم وتسرب البيانات الناتج عنها. التحليل: الجهات السعودية والخليجية التي تستخدم الوكلاء في الحكومة والصحة والبنوك والبنية التحتية تحتاج إلى صلاحيات محدودة، وسجلات تدقيق، وإبلاغ إلزامي عن الحوادث، وتحديد واضح للمسؤولية مع مزودي التقنية. ما نتابع الرد الأميركي الرسمي على المقترح الإيراني، تنفيذ الصين لتعهداتها بشأن هرمز، الهجمات الحوثية وطبيعة الدعم التركي والباكستاني للسعودية، حركة الناقلات وأسعار التأمين، الضربات الروسية على الصناعة الأوكرانية، وأي إجراءات رقابية بعد تسريب بيانات وكلاء الذكاء الاصطناعي فاصل اصنع عالمك الخاص.

story-3ae9003ebf3dedfd9969a183.content: 🚨 PACIFIC WEATHER JOURNAL | RACHEL IS NOW ON THE EDGE OF HURRICANE STRENGTH AS POLO FADES INLAND 🌀 September 29, 2026 | SpaceTracker Advanced Weather Journal 🌎 LIVE monitoring: https://t.co/6Ul2gIGlrX I analyzed the full 4-minute 26-second SpaceTracker recording. The sequence begins over Cabo San Lucas and La Paz after Hurricane Polo's passage, follows the remaining circulation northward, then moves south along Mexico's Pacific coast where a much more important development is underway: The enormous storm with the brilliant red, black and purple cloud shield is Tropical Storm Rachel. And Rachel has changed substantially today. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 🌀 RACHEL IS ONLY A FEW MPH FROM BECOMING A HURRICANE At the newest NHC advisory, issued 3:00 PM CST September 29, Rachel was centered near 16.0°N, 105.7°W, about 435 km west-southwest of Lázaro Cárdenas and 490 km south of Cabo Corrientes. Maximum sustained winds have increased to: 70 mph | 110 km/h Minimum pressure: 989 mb Movement: northwest at 12 mph | 19 km/h Hurricane strength begins at 74 mph, meaning Rachel is now extremely close to crossing that threshold. National Hurricane Center ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 🛰️ WHAT YOU ARE SEEING IN THE VIDEO IS NOT A GIANT EYE This is probably the most important part of the analysis. During the close zoom in your recording, Rachel develops an enormous purple-centered circular feature surrounded by black, red and yellow. Visually, it looks almost like an enormous hurricane eye. But it is not an eye. The SpaceTracker satellite layer is using enhanced infrared cloud-top temperatures. The purple region represents exceptionally cold and extremely high thunderstorm clouds. NHC reports Rachel currently has a massive convective burst with cloud tops colder than -85°C. That burst is actually displaced slightly south of the storm's circulation center. National Hurricane Center So what the video captures is arguably more interesting: We are watching Rachel attempt to construct its inner hurricane core. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ ✈️ NOAA HURRICANE HUNTERS JUST FLEW INTO RACHEL Today's update is based on much more than satellite estimates. A NOAA P-3 Hurricane Hunter aircraft entered Rachel and measured 700-mb flight-level winds of 66 knots. A dropsonde released near the radius of maximum wind recorded approximately 75-knot winds, while an experimental uncrewed aircraft operating much closer to the ocean surface also measured winds reaching about 75 knots at 975 mb. Analysis of those observations supports surface sustained winds close to hurricane strength. National Hurricane Center That direct sampling is why NHC has increased Rachel to 70 mph. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ ⚡ THE FORECAST HAS CHANGED SIGNIFICANTLY Earlier forecasts called for gradual strengthening. Now NHC explicitly forecasts a period of: RAPID INTENSIFICATION The official intensity forecast currently takes Rachel from: 70 mph now → 80 mph tonight → 100 mph Wednesday → 115 mph early Thursday → approximately 120 mph | 195 km/h Thursday afternoon That would make Rachel a Category 3 major hurricane. National Hurricane Center ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 🌊 WHY COULD RACHEL INTENSIFY SO QUICKLY? Several atmospheric ingredients are suddenly becoming much more favorable. Until now, northeasterly wind shear has been pushing Rachel's strongest thunderstorms away from its low-level center. But that shear is decreasing. Forecast guidance indicates vertical shear could fall below roughly 15 knots during the next 24 hours. At the same time, ocean observations along Rachel's immediate track show water temperatures around an extremely warm 29–30°C. National Hurricane Center Warm ocean. Less wind shear. Increasing vertical alignment. Deep tropical moisture. A tightening circulation. Put those together and Rachel's atmospheric heat engine can become dramatically more efficient. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 🔬 YOUR VIDEO MAY BE CAPTURING THE TRANSITION BEFORE AN EYE FORMS Across the close-up sequence, the convection becomes increasingly concentrated. There is still no clean warm eye surrounded by an eyewall like we saw with Hurricane Nolo. Instead, Rachel currently looks like a huge boiling convective shield. That fits NHC's aircraft analysis: the circulation is becoming more vertically aligned, but its strongest convection remains displaced somewhat from the actual center. National Hurricane Center The next visual milestone to watch is therefore clear: Does a small warm opening begin developing inside that enormous cold cloud shield? If it does, that could signal the construction of a true hurricane eye and eyewall. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 📏 RACHEL IS ALREADY A LARGE TROPICAL CYCLONE Rachel's strongest inner core is still organizing, but its broader circulation is substantial. NHC says tropical-storm-force winds extend outward as far as 185 miles | 295 km from the center. National Hurricane Center Because the wind field is asymmetric, that does not mean Rachel is a perfect 590-km-wide circle. But it does illustrate the scale. The dangerous weather footprint extends far beyond whatever eye may eventually develop. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 🇲🇽 THE CENTER SHOULD REMAIN OFFSHORE, BUT MEXICO IS STILL EXPOSED Current guidance keeps Rachel moving roughly parallel to southwestern Mexico rather than taking the core directly inland. A Tropical Storm Warning covers the coast from Punta San Telmo to Playa Pérula, while a watch extends farther north toward Cabo Corrientes. National Hurricane Center Outer bands can still deliver significant impacts far from the circulation center. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 🌧️ 4 TO 8 INCHES OF RAIN | ISOLATED 12-INCH TOTALS NHC currently forecasts approximately 4–8 inches of rainfall, with isolated totals reaching 12 inches, across coastal portions of: Guerrero Michoacán Colima Jalisco Steep terrain makes those rainfall totals particularly important because intense tropical rain can rapidly produce flash flooding and mudslides. National Hurricane Center Large swells from Rachel are also expected to spread northward along Mexico's Pacific coast, creating dangerous surf and rip currents. National Hurricane Center ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 🌊 THEN POLO ENTERS THE SCIENTIFIC STORY AGAIN One of the most fascinating aspects of Rachel's forecast involves Hurricane Polo. Rachel is following relatively close to part of Polo's previous ocean track. A powerful hurricane churns the ocean violently. Its winds mix the upper ocean and pull cooler water upward from below. The result is known as a: HURRICANE COLD WAKE NHC says Rachel is initially forecast to remain north of Polo's coldest wake, over water still around 29–30°C. That helps explain the new rapid-intensification forecast. National Hurricane Center ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ ❄️ BUT RACHEL MAY EVENTUALLY HIT POLO'S COLD WATER Farther west, ocean drifters are measuring temperatures of only about 26–27°C in water disturbed by Polo. Rachel is forecast to slow down and eventually cross that cooler region. That could substantially reduce the oceanic energy available to the hurricane. NHC therefore forecasts Rachel to peak as a major hurricane and then begin weakening roughly 60–96 hours from now. National Hurricane Center That creates an unusual meteorological storyline: Polo may help weaken the storm that formed behind it. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 🌀 MEANWHILE, POLO ITSELF IS RAPIDLY DISAPPEARING The beginning of your recording revisits Cabo San Lucas, La Paz and Mulegé. Satellite enhancement still shows impressive cloud structures across Baja California and northwestern Mexico. But Polo's center is no longer there. Polo crossed the Gulf of California and made its second landfall just east of Guaymas, Sonora. It has weakened to a 65-mph tropical storm inland and is expected to lose its surface circulation tonight. National Hurricane Center That explains the striking contrast in your video. At Cabo San Lucas your local layer shows mostly sunny conditions around 32°C, while residual tropical cloud bands remain visible farther north. At La Paz the local view is sunny while deep convection remains visible on satellite. The hurricane itself has already moved inland. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 🇺🇸 POLO'S WIND WILL DIE — ITS WATER WILL NOT Polo's circulation is collapsing over land. Its tropical moisture is continuing northeast. NHC expects the remnants to move across northwestern Mexico toward southern New Mexico and far western Texas, interacting with a mid-latitude trough. That combination can generate heavy rainfall, flash flooding and strong gusty winds even after Polo is no longer officially a tropical cyclone. National Hurricane Center This is an important reminder: Hurricanes can stop being hurricanes long before their impacts stop. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ ⛈️ THEN THE VIDEO MOVES INTO GUATEMALA Near the end of the recording, the tour moves across Panimaché and Volcán de Fuego. The satellite layer shows exceptionally deep thunderstorm convection, while the local panels report thunderstorms and very high cloud cover. These cells should not be confused with Rachel's core. By this point, the video has moved hundreds of kilometres eastward into Central America. They are separate convective storms within the broader tropical environment. The brilliant red and black infrared enhancement again represents very cold, high cloud tops, not a hurricane eye. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 🔥 VOLCÁN DE FUEGO DISAPPEARS BEHIND THE WEATHER The final local camera view near Volcán de Fuego's southeast flank is almost completely obscured by low cloud, rain and mist. That is a useful reminder about combining different observational systems. Satellite imagery tells us what is happening high in the atmosphere. Local webcams show what is actually visible from the ground. And numerical models estimate conditions between observation points. Together they provide a far more complete weather picture than any single source. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 🚨 THE BIGGEST STORY IN THIS VIDEO IS NOW RACHEL Twenty-four hours ago, Rachel was a much less organized tropical storm. Tonight it is sitting at 70 mph, only 4 mph below hurricane strength. Hurricane Hunters have now sampled the inner circulation directly. Wind shear is decreasing. Ocean temperatures remain around 29–30°C. The storm's core is becoming better aligned. And NHC has raised the forecast to a 120-mph major hurricane within roughly 48 hours. story-3dac88bd3e6cbcb8f97e8f3a.content: Official Document TitlesThe Hague Convention on the Regulation and Limitation of Artificial Intelligence in Armed ConflictsThe Hague Protocol on Lethal Autonomous Weapon Systems and Military AIThe Hague Declaration on Artificial Intelligence and the Principles of Digital WarfareProtocol V to the Hague Convention: Rules Governing Algorithmic WarfareTreaty Framework and ArticlesPreambleThe High Contracting Parties,Conscious of the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence and autonomous technologies in the military domain,Determined to prevent the dehumanization of warfare and to ensure that the use of force remains under strict ethical and legal boundaries,Reaffirming that the principles of international humanitarian law must apply to all new methods and means of warfare,Have agreed as follows:Article 1: The Principle of Meaningful Human ControlThe use of autonomous systems capable of selecting and engaging targets without human intervention is strictly prohibited.Any decision to execute a lethal strike or use force resulting in injury, death, or structural destruction must remain under meaningful human control. The final authority to deploy force rests solely with a human operator.Article 2: Prohibition of Untraceable Algorithms ("Black Box" Exclusion)High Contracting Parties shall not deploy military artificial intelligence systems whose decision-making logic cannot be audited, explained, or reverse-engineered by human experts.The operational source code and telemetry of military AI must be securely logged and preserved for post-operation legal review.Article 3: Target Discrimination and the Principle of DistinctionMilitary AI algorithms must demonstrate a reliable, high-precision capability to distinguish between lawful combatants and protected persons, including civilians, hors de combat, and medical personnel.If an AI system encounters environmental degradation, sensor degradation, or unexpected data anomalies that impair its ability to discriminate targets, it must immediately abort the mission or revert to manual human control.Article 4: Criminal Liability and Chain of CommandArtificial intelligence systems cannot be held legally or criminally responsible for violations of international humanitarian law.Criminal liability for war crimes resulting from algorithmic errors, malfunction, or unlawful deployment shall be attributed directly to the military commanders who authorized the deployment and the software developers or state entities who knowingly programmed unlawful parameters.Would you like to expand this document further into:Article 5 regarding Cyber Warfare and AI-driven autonomous cyber-attacks?A specific Signatory and Ratification clause?A set of Definitions for terms like "Autonomous System" and "Algorithmic Target Acquisition"?

story-40267db92fd1f80bcedb659b.content: NEW ANALYSIS: U.S.-Saudi Arabia Cooperation on Enrichment: Framework for a Black Box There is lots to digest in the U.S.-Saudi Arabia nuclear cooperation package of agreements, minute, and unclassified Nonproliferation Assessment. We started with trying to understand how and under what provisions the United States could provide Saudi Arabia with an enrichment facility. Key findings below: The language appears deliberately structured so that a U.S. designed, built, and operated enrichment facility can be deployed in Saudi Arabia without automatically transferring the centrifuge technology embodied in that facility. Details were not provided, but in such an arrangement the U.S. would be expected to retain control of centrifuge design, production, assembly, maintenance, and physical access. This is in line with what The Wall Street Journal earlier reported as a secretive “black box” facility, “avoiding the transfer of sensitive enrichment technology” to Saudi Arabia. The agreement creates the framework to establish a black box centrifuge plant but establishing that facility will require many future agreements between the United States and Saudi Arabia, not just the two-year Joint Enrichment and Conversion Study (JECS). In terms of proliferation implications, several things need to happen independently, namely restricting access to the centrifuges and centrifuge technology. The public agreement does not yet clearly establish physical access restrictions to the former. It does provide mechanisms to restrict access to much of the latter. Most notably, it categorically excludes the transfer of Restricted Data (RD) and classified information, which covers many areas related to centrifuge design, specification, production, and operation. A potential loophole is that the agreement explicitly permits transfers of centrifuge sensitive nuclear technology (SNT) under certain circumstances. The agreement allows SNT transfer to support the Joint Enrichment and Conversion Study (JECS) or upon written agreement of the parties. Therefore, the legal architecture of the agreement is not a categorical prohibition on ever transferring or teaching information on enrichment facilities. The public package is silent on the question of whether Saudi Arabia could pursue its own centrifuge research and development programs while also receiving a U.S.-supplied enrichment plant, including SNT, from the United States. It does say that there is an “understanding that any SNT transferred for purposes of the JECS could not be used by the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia for other purposes,” but this still needs to be put in writing in a yet-to-be negotiated “exchange of diplomatic notes” and raises questions on verification. Based on our past research and current AI-assisted searches of open sources, we found little evidence in the publicly visible scientific literature of significant or sustained Saudi Arabian indigenous research on the specialized technologies required for gas-centrifuge enrichment. This suggests that if Saudi Arabia wants to independently acquire gas centrifuge enrichment capabilities in the near-to-medium term, it will need to launch a major domestic program to do so or obtain such a capability via foreign technology and training. The latter could involve covert assistance from centrifuge suppliers, such as Pakistan, or exploitation of opportunities presented by cooperation with the United States. Overall, the idea of a black box enrichment plant is attractive. To determine whether this package of agreements and subsequent ones will achieve a secure black box, many questions need to be answered on the extent of Saudi Arabia’s involvement in building, maintaining, and operating the enrichment facility and the risk of proliferation. A list of 21 questions that should be asked by Congress is included in our report: https://t.co/G4jtURAQGe
